quotes.text: Learn to accept Australia BECS Direct Debit payments.
This article has multiple variants. Fetch one of the following URLs to view specific content for your use case:

old_evidence.text: BECS Direct Debit is a [delayed notification](https://docs.stripe.com/payments/payment-methods.md#payment-notification) payment method, which means that funds aren’t immediately available.
Use [BecsDebitWidget](https://stripe.dev/stripe-android/payments-core/com.stripe.android.view/-becs-debit-widget/index.html), Stripe’s prebuilt BECS payment details collection UI
The PaymentIntent status transitions from `processing` to `succeeded`. The mandate status remains `active`.

findings: The November capture is an index with six parameterized variant routes: Checkout, Elements Checkout Sessions, Elements Payment Intents, iOS, Android, React Native (new raw lines 9-20). It gives no variant-specific prerequisites, payment behavior, state machine, test behavior, or deprecation statement. The diff deletes the prior detailed body and adds navigation (diff lines 3-20, 2375-2382), so this is a capture/presentation change, not proved product change.

These remain historical evidence only.

The old Android prose/example disagreement at old raw lines 1322-1357 and 1421 needs a separately authorized and pinned variant or SDK authority before an executable call is recommended; this packet does not resolve it.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/au-becs-debit/accept-a-payment, the complete November capture establishes the page's purpose and six selectable Checkout, Elements Checkout Sessions, Elements Payment Intents, iOS, Android, and React Native variant URLs, with no detailed prerequisites or payment-state claims (new raw lines 5-20). The May 2 capture supplies dated detail: Australian customers and AUD Checkout line items, server-created Sessions or PaymentIntents, client payment/mandate collection and confirmation, Account v2 versus Customer v1 reuse identities, and delayed processing before succeeded or failed (old raw lines 18-49, 193-205, 239-243, 890-950, 1027-1054, 1752-1758). source-stripe-au-becs-accept-payment.md preserves several branches but omits React Native and the distinct Elements Payment Intents route, misnames the Android widget/call, and calls a processing-to-succeeded test immediate (source lines 13-48; old raw lines 1088-1094, 1322-1357, 114-117).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/au-becs-debit/accept-a-payment, the observed change is presentation/navigation: November's index links six parameterized variants but supplies no replacement integration content or deprecation evidence (new raw lines 9-20; diff lines 3-20, 2375-2382). The detailed May 2 instructions remain dated historical claims: AUD and mode compatibility, conditional Accounts v2 availability, separate Session/PaymentIntent flows, old UI/SDK versions, best-effort target_date, mandate and failure behavior, and delayed payment finality (old raw lines 22-36, 197-205, 318-349, 1023-1054, 135-146). source-stripe-au-becs-accept-payment.md needs a reciprocal warning that its Android names and immediate-success shorthand conflict with its pinned old raw (source lines 39-42, 48; old raw lines 1088-1094, 1322-1357, 114-117, 706); old iOS prose and code also differ on the form class name (old raw lines 729, 840). No bank execution, variant access, live eligibility, or successful payment is established by this snapshot.
